newsitem.title: USA: Jones Medical shares tumble after earnings warning.
newsitem.headline: Jones Medical shares tumble after earnings warning.

text.p: Stock in St. Louis-based Jones Medical Industries Inc. plummeted more than 35 percent Monday after the drug company said its second-quarter earnings would come in well short of Wall Street estimates.
The company's stock fell $15.50 to close at $27.875 on Nasdaq, where it was the most active stock on volume of more than 13 million shares and the second biggest percentage loser.
Late last week, the company announced it expected earnings of about 20 cents per share, far below the 28 cents a share predicted by Wall Street analysts.

The earnings shortfall stemmed from aggressive wholesale buying of two top-selling drugs -- Tapazole and Levoxyl -- ahead of an April 1 price hike, said company Chairman Dennis Jones in a conference call.
The price increase was announced March 24. "In retrospect, we probably gave (wholesalers) too much opportunity to take advantage of some bargain buying in late March," Jones said.
"We understand what is happening and we believe that third and fourth quarter 1997 will not have the dynamics of the two quarters that we've just discussed," Jones said.
